statement: Let n = len(nums). For integers i and j, call the split (i,j) beautiful exactly when 1 <= i < j < n and either (A) i <= j - i and for every k with 0 <= k < i, nums[k] = nums[i+k], or (B) j - i <= n - j and for every k with 0 <= k < j - i, nums[i+k] = nums[j+k]. The function returns a result r and r equals the number of beautiful pairs (i,j).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, access out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: Let N be the number of integer pairs (i,j) such that 1 <= i < j < len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= N.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: If len(nums) <= 2, then the function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 1 if nums[0] = nums[1] or nums[1] = nums[2], and r = 0 otherwise.

Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of integer pairs (i,j) such that 1 <= i < j < n, j - i <= n - j, and for every k with 0 <= k < j - i, nums[i+k] = nums[j+k].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000, for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50, and for every i with 1 <= i < len(nums), nums[0] != nums[i].

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000, for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50, and for every p,q with 0 <= p < q < len(nums), nums[p] != nums[q].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if r > 0 then there exist integers i and j with 1 <= i < j < len(nums) such that either (i <= j - i and for every k with 0 <= k < i, nums[k] = nums[i+k]) or (j - i <= len(nums) - j and for every k with 0 <= k < j - i, nums[i+k] = nums[j+k]).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: If beautiful_splits(nums) returns r and beautiful_splits(alt) returns r_alt, then r = r_alt.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000, for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50, and alt is an array such that len(alt) = len(nums), for every k with 0 <= k < len(alt), 0 <= alt[k] <= 50, and for every p,q with 0 <= p < len(nums) and 0 <= q < len(nums), nums[p] = nums[q] if and only if alt[p] = alt[q].

statement: For every integer x with 0 <= x <= 50, let ext be the array of length len(nums)+1 such that ext[k] = nums[k] for 0 <= k < len(nums) and ext[len(nums)] = x. Whenever beautiful_splits(nums) returns r and beautiful_splits(ext) returns r_ext, r_ext >= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 4999 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: For every integer x with 0 <= x <= 50, let ext be the array of length len(nums)+1 such that ext[k] = nums[k] for 0 <= k < len(nums) and ext[len(nums)] = x. Whenever beautiful_splits(nums) returns r and beautiful_splits(ext) returns r_ext, r_ext - r <= 2*(len(nums)-1).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 4999 and for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000, for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50, len(nums) >= 3, and (nums[0] = nums[1] or nums[len(nums)-2] = nums[len(nums)-1]).

statement: Let pre be the slice nums[0..k). If beautiful_splits(pre) returns r_pre and beautiful_splits(nums) returns r, then r_pre <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000, for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 0 <= nums[k] <= 50, and 1 <= k <= len(nums).
